html:
The cathedral of the Archdiocese of Mexico, on the main square of Mexico City, the largest cathedral in the Americas. Building began in 1573 and went on for about 240 years, until 1813.

It stands over part of the sacred precinct of Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital, close to the ruins of the Templo Mayor. Stones from the old temples were used in the first church on the site. Placing the cathedral there was a clear statement that Christianity had replaced the old gods.

Because it took so long, its styles change as you look: Renaissance in its plan, baroque in its altars and much of the front, and neoclassical in the dome and finishing touches added by Manuel Tolsá. Its Altar of the Kings is a famous gilded baroque altarpiece.

Mexico City sits on the soft bed of a drained lake, and the heavy building has long been sinking unevenly. Large engineering works in the 1990s were needed to steady it.
sum: The cathedral of the Archdiocese of Mexico, on the main square of Mexico City, the largest cathedral in the Americas. Building began in 1573 and went on for about 240 years, until 1813.
